title: Definition of Ready and work-order template: require durable anchors, not line numbers (RFC B-P1)
description:
groom-beads groomed 17 beads that bead-bonanza then executed in one sprint over
a single skill bundle (run 1786562615-17). Fourteen of the seventeen cited
file:line positions in their Description or Design, and EVERY cited position had
moved by the time its bead was dispatched, because earlier beads in the same run
edited the same files. The sprint's own analysis calls this its dominant
friction.

Six beads recorded it independently, in their own words:

- b13: "the bead's cited line numbers (pre-flight-check.sh:269,:284,:455,
  :494-495; SKILL.md:1106-1113; bb-close-bead.sh:159-165) had all moved -- four
  earlier-sprint beads (q1h, td1, 9p4, 8mv) touched pre-flight-check.sh. Located
  each effect by content..."
- 8ef.1: "Every line number in the description is stale, as warned..."
- 8ef.2: "every line number in the description had moved, but every named
  passage was still findable by content... The offsets are roughly uniform
  (-72 lines...)"
- 8ef.3: "the bead's Category-D line-number citations were mostly stale, as
  warned."
- new: "Every line number in the Design was stale. recovery.md was 17,277 bytes
  / 251 lines, not 18,767 / 263 -- the cited ranges... all shifted."
- b5z: "Every cited line range was stale. Phase 2.5 was SKILL.md:494-726, not
  :559-818..."

The Definition of Ready asks for this at check 1: a Problem statement "SHALL
name concrete anchors -- file paths, function/class names, endpoints, tables,
user-facing behavior". A line number reads as the most concrete anchor
available, so a groomer reaching for concreteness reaches for it. The check does
not say that concreteness and durability are different properties.

Nothing was mis-edited, because the orchestrator improvised a mitigation -- it
added "locate by content, not by line number, and report the drift" to every
dispatch prompt. That is why this is a snag and not a blocker, but it was
per-run and unprescribed. The failure mode when it is NOT anticipated is not a
mis-edit; it is silence: an agent that trusts a stale range edits the wrong
region, or reports the cited content "already fixed" because what is at those
lines now is something else.

Source: rfcs/inbox/groom-beads/rfc-self-line-anchors-rot-across-a-sprint.md, P1.
Approved adopt-now at triage on 2026-08-13, widened per Design.
design:
## Extent -- this is TWO source files, not one

The RFC proposes changing only work-order-definition-of-ready.md. A triage
extent check (grep -rn 'concrete anchors' plugin/ specs/) found the phrase in
two spec-owned sources, each with vendored copies -- six files total:

  plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-definition-of-ready.md        (source)
  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/shared/work-order-defin...       (vendored)
  plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-defin...        (vendored)
  plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md                   (source)
  plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-template.md     (vendored)
  plugin/skills/groom-feature-blueprint/references/shared/work-order-... (vendored)

In the DoR the phrase sits in check 1, under the heading "### 1. Self-contained
Problem statement (the fresh-agent test)", in the sentence beginning "It SHALL
name concrete anchors". In the template it sits in the `## Problem` instruction
block, in the sentence beginning "reads first, so it SHALL survive the
fresh-agent test -- name concrete anchors". Locate both by those phrases.

Changing the DoR alone leaves work-order-template.md telling an author to "name
concrete anchors (file paths, symbols, endpoints, tables, user-facing
behavior)" with no durability qualifier -- and the template is what an author
writes INTO, so it is read at least as often as the gate. Both sources change.

## 1. work-order-definition-of-ready.md, check 1 ("### 1. Self-contained Problem
statement (the fresh-agent test)")

After the existing "concrete anchors" sentence, add:

> An anchor SHALL be durable under edits to the same file. File paths, symbol
> names, headings and short quoted strings are durable; line numbers and line
> ranges are not, and neither are byte counts or item counts. WHERE a work order
> names a position, it SHALL name the content at that position -- quote the
> heading or the first few words -- and MAY give a line number only as a
> convenience alongside it. In a queue where several orders touch one file,
> every line number is stale before the second order is dispatched.

## 2. work-order-template.md, the Problem instruction block

Add a short durability clause to the "name concrete anchors" guidance -- quote
the content at a position, line numbers only alongside it. Keep it to a clause
or two; the template's instruction blocks are terse by convention and the full
rule belongs in the DoR.

## 3. Regenerate, never hand-edit, the vendored copies

The sources live in the spec skill. Run scripts/sync-shared-references.sh to
regenerate, then scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check to verify no drift.
Never edit a file under references/shared/ directly.

## Version bumps (this bead owns both)

- work-order-definition-of-ready.md frontmatter version 1.3 -> 1.4
- work-order-template.md instruction-block "Version: 1.4" -> 1.5 (this template
  versions in its instruction block, not in frontmatter)

Bump the SOURCES and let the regeneration carry the bumps into the vendored
copies.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] work-order-definition-of-ready.md check 1 states that an anchor SHALL be durable under edits to the same file, naming file paths/symbols/headings/short quoted strings as durable and line numbers, line ranges, byte counts and item counts as not
- [ ] It requires naming the content at a position, permitting a line number only as a convenience alongside it
- [ ] work-order-template.md's Problem instruction block carries a durability clause consistent with the DoR rule
- [ ] Both changes were made to the spec-skill sources, not to any references/shared/ copy
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh was run and scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exits clean
- [ ] work-order-definition-of-ready.md version is 1.4 and all vendored copies agree
- [ ] work-order-template.md instruction-block Version is 1.5 and all vendored copies agree

metadata.tier_reason: Two spec-owned sources plus a regeneration step and two different version-property conventions; getting the vendored copies right is where this goes wrong.

dependencies.title: Adopt the seven approved changes from the 2026-08-13 RFC triage
dependencies.description:
Triage of two self-authored RFCs on 2026-08-13 approved five proposals for
immediate adoption. This epic carries them.

Sources:
- rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-report-citations-and-batch-base.md (P1a, P2, P5)
- rfcs/inbox/groom-beads/rfc-self-line-anchors-rot-across-a-sprint.md (P1, P2)

Both RFCs carry origin: self and model: claude-opus-5, and were triaged by the
same model. RFC A's P2 ratifies a decision its own author made mid-run. No
independent project has corroborated any of it.

A-P4 was approved on 2026-08-13 in reshaped form and is in this epic: triage
found the expiries were caused by the tool default timeout_ms of five minutes,
not by a 30-minute cap, and the fix is persistent: true rather than re-arming.
The cap figure the RFC reported is deliberately not adopted.

One triage-originated change (T1, record the run effort setting in the dispatch
manifest) was approved on 2026-08-13 and is in this epic. No reporter proposed
it; the reasoning is triage own.

Three further proposals (A-P1b citation checker, A-P3 gate-output redirect,
A-P6 verification-by-reconstruction) are held for human review and are NOT in
this epic. A-P1b in particular is a likely successor to
this work: it depends on the per-bead finding ids that A-P1a introduces.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All seven approved changes implemented and verified in the tree
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md bumped exactly once (1.4 -> 1.5), by
      the dispatch-manifest effort bead, which lands last of the five editing it
- [ ] No version property was added to any bead-bonanza reference file; the
      skill versions as a bundle
- [ ] plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md bumped exactly once (1.2 -> 1.3)
- [ ] work-order-definition-of-ready.md 1.3 -> 1.4 and work-order-template.md
      instruction-block Version 1.4 -> 1.5, with vendored copies regenerated
      and scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check clean
- [ ] Plugin version bumped MINOR once, after the held-for-review items are
      resolved (0.17.0 -> 0.18.0 if nothing further lands)
- [ ] Resolutions written into both RFCs, disclosing same-model authorship and
      triage, and both RFCs renumbered into rfcs/retired/ with status retired
- [ ] One row per RFC appended to rfcs/retro-log.md
